why: Week 7 reference decision: COVERED. Supply hose burst, discovered within two hours, failed hose kept. E-17 exception for sudden and accidental (Clause 1(a), 14 days or fewer) applies. 8,400 - 1,000 excess.

Week 7 reference decision: DENIED. First notice reads like a supply-line loss (E-17), but the plumber's note puts the leak at six to eight weeks. That is continuous seepage over 14 days, E-18, excluded absolutely.

Week 7 reference decision: DENIED. Notes reveal the creek overtopped and water came through the window wells: surface water / flood, E-15, no exception. HO-0820 covers backup through drains or sump only, not surface water.

Week 7 reference decision: COVERED. Notes reveal sewer backup through the floor drain: E-16 would exclude, but HO-0820 Clause 2 overrides it up to 10,000 per event with a 1,000 deductible. min(14,200, 10,000) - 1,000.
Week 7 reference decision: COVERED. Sump failure could fall under E-51, but the utility report shows a 16.5 hour outage, over the 12 hour exception. Covered under HO-0820. min(6,300, 10,000) - 1,000.

Week 7 reference decision: DENIED. Vacant 45 days (over 30), so E-61 applies. Water was shut off and drained, which would trigger the exception, but DP-0703 Clause 4: first inspection was 20 days after the tenancy ended, not within 7, which voids the exception.
Week 7 reference decision: DENIED. Metal roof, denting only, still sheds water. E-22, excluded absolutely.
Week 7 reference decision: UNDETERMINED. No adjuster notes. Cause of the kitchen water and its duration are unknown, so neither E-17 nor E-18 can be decided.

Week 7 reference decision: COVERED. Notes reveal a home business with 38,000 gross receipts (over 5,000), so the stolen items are business property. HO-0509 Clause 2 sublimit of 2,500 on premises. min(6,000, 2,500) - 500.

Week 7 reference decision: UNDETERMINED. Leak start is unknown, so sudden and accidental (E-17 exception) versus continuous seepage (E-18) cannot be decided, and the failed fitting was discarded (HO-0304 Clause 4 may void the exception).
Loss 2024-08-11: HO-0304 ed. 03-24 is in force. Surface water is excluded under E-15 with no exception. The 2025 Storm Ingress Allowance did not exist yet.
Loss 2024-12-31, the last day before the 2025 edition: ed. 03-24 is in force, E-15 excludes surface water absolutely.
Loss 2025-01-01, the first day of ed. 01-25: storm ingress (door, 58 mm) is the E-15 exception, paid up to the 5,000 Storm Ingress Allowance (Clause 5) less the deductible.
Loss 2025-03-14 under ed. 01-25: storm ingress through a window in a 66 mm storm - E-15 exception, Storm Ingress Allowance 5,000, deductible 750.
Loss 2025-02-10 under ed. 01-25: river flood is not storm ingress, so the new exception does not reach it - E-15 still excludes.
The only term ended 2024-09-30 (cancelled); the loss on 2024-10-12 falls outside it.
The policy incepted 2024-11-01, four days after the 2024-10-28 loss.
Gap between terms: the 2024 term ended 2024-12-31 and the renewal began 2025-01-05; the loss on 2025-01-03 is in neither.
Sewer backup: E-16 is overridden by the HO-0820 Clause 2 grant - sub-limit 10,000 per event with HO-0820's own 1,000 deductible (not the 500 policy deductible); dwelling limit 380,000.
Business property away from the residence premises: HO-0509 Clause 2 sub-limit 500; deductible 250; the limit it sits within is Coverage C personal property, 140,000.
Ordinance or law: HO-0612 raises the limit to 25 percent of Coverage A, so the sub-limit is 87,500 within the 350,000 dwelling limit; deductible 1,000; no pollutant cost is claimed.
A homeowners policy on the insured's own home does not reach a tenant-occupied condo elsewhere; a dwelling-fire policy would be needed and none is on file (Week 6 C13, labelled NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS).
The policy carries HO-0415 ed. 05-23, which is not in the wording library; ed. 01-24 must not be applied in its place (Week 6 C12).
HO-0304 ed. 03-24 took effect on 2024-03-01, after this 2024-02-10 loss; the edition in force on the loss date is not in the library, so ed. 03-24 must not be applied to it.
Empty 49 days: E-61 applies; the shut-off-and-drain exception is voided by the Clause 4 duty to inspect within 7 days, which was not done.
